title: CHAPTER 2: SENSATION AND PERCEPTION
content:
ውድና የተወደዳችሁ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 💖👋 እንደምን አላችሁ? እኔ ደህና ነኝ ናፍቆቶቼ። ዛሬ ደግሞ የGeneral Psychology (Psyc 1011) Chapter 2 Part 2 Tutorial ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። ይህ ክፍል ለአብዛኞቻችሁ አዲስ በመሆኑና ከፍተኛ የፈተና ሽፋን ስላለው፣ ስለ Perception (የአእምሮ ግንዛቤ) እና እንዴት መረጃዎችን እንደምንመርጥ፣ እንደምናደራጅና ትርጉም እንደምንሰጥ በጥልቀትና በምስሎች (Visual Displays) አስደግፈን አዘጋጅተነዋል👇


2.3. Perception

You have seen earlier that perception is a fundamental meaning-making psychological process. Now you will study more about this active cognitive process that characterizes human intelligent life. It helps you understand the major characteristics of the perceptual process: selectivity of perception, form perception, depth perception, perceptual constancy, and perceptual illusion.

2.3.1. Selectivity of perception: Attention

Note that at any given time, your sensory organs are continuously bombarded by countless environmental stimuli (sounds, visual cues, smells, body tactile signals). Yet you only consciously perceive a tiny fraction of them. Were you aware of, for example, the ambient noise in your room or the weight of your shoes on your feet until you read this exact sentence? You likely were not. Yet sensory inputs from the environment were registering upon your sensory receptors all the time. In fact, you were actively attending to one of such incoming inputs while completely filtering out or ignoring the other background noises. Such selective perception is technically termed attention.

Attention is therefore defined as the active perceptual process that selects specific environmental sensory inputs for inclusion in your conscious experience or immediate awareness at any given time, while systematically ignoring or suppressing others.

Focus and Margin
The selectivity of perception implies that our total field of conscious experience is continuously divided into two dynamic zones: "Focus" and "Margin."
• Focus: Events, stimuli, or objects that you are perceiving clearly and sharply occupy the central focus of your immediate conscious experience.
• Margin: Other background items or stimuli that you are perceiving only dimly, vaguely, or subconsciously sit in the margin of your awareness.

Module Example: Consider watching a high-stakes football game. While you are dimly and vaguely aware of the general tangle of players on the field (Margin), your sharp attention is strictly focused on the ball carrier and his fast movement towards the goal (Focus). At the very same time, sensory nerve signals are coming into your brain from your cold feet touching the ground or the loud crowd shouting in the stadium background. You are probably completely unaware of these sensory inputs until the play is finished and the whistle blows. This clearly illustrates that attention is constantly shifting over time. What occupies the focus of your attention at one moment may shift into the margin the next moment, and vice versa.

👉 Selectivity & Attention:
በማንኛውም ቅፅበት በዙሪያችን አያሌ ድምፆች፣ ምስሎች፣ የሙቀት መጠኖች እና ሽታዎች (Stimuli) አሉ። ነገር ግን የሰው ልጅ አእምሮ ውስን አቅም ስላለው ሁሉንም በአንድ ጊዜ ማስተናገድ አይችልም። ስለዚህ አስፈላጊውን መርጦ ለአንዱ ብቻ ትኩረት ይሰጣል፤ ይሄ መርጦ የማስተናገድ ሂደት Attention (ትኩረት) ይባላል።
• Focus (ዋና ትኩረት): በዚህ ቅፅበት በከፍተኛ ጥራት እያያችሁት፣ እያነበባችሁት ወይም እየሰማችሁት ያለ ዋና ነገር ነው። (ለምሳሌ፡ አሁን ይሄን የትምህርት ኖት በዓይናችሁ ማንበባችሁ Focus ነው)።
• Margin (የዳር/የጀርባ ትኩረት): በዙሪያችሁ ያሉ ግን አእምሯችሁ ከጀርባ ያደረጋቸውና በደበዘዘ መልኩ የሚሰሙ/ሚታዩ ነገሮች ናቸው። (ለምሳሌ፡ ከውጪ የሚሰማ የሰዎች ወሬ፣ የደጋፊዎች ጩኸት፣ ወይም የለበሳችሁት ልብስ በቆዳችሁ ላይ የሚፈጥረው ስሜት)። Focus እና Margin ቋሚ አይደሉም፤ ሁሌም ይለዋወጣሉ (Constantly shifting)። ለምሳሌ ለረጅም ሰዓት በጽኑ ካጠናችሁ በኋላ ድካም ሲሰማችሁ፣ የጥናቱ ትኩረት ወደ Margin ይወርዳል፤ በአንፃሩ የውጪው ድምፅ ወይም የሰውነታችሁ ድካም ወደ Focus ይመጣል።

🤔 Case Question 1:
Sara is reading her psychology module in the dorm. Her roommates are talking loudly, and music is playing outside. Sara is entirely absorbed in her reading and doesn't hear what her roommates are saying. Suddenly, one roommate drops a glass, breaking it loudly. Sara jumps up and looks at the glass.
Question: In terms of perception, what were the module, the roommates' talk, and the breaking glass representing at different times?

Answer: The module was initially the Focus, while the talking and music were the Margin. When the glass broke, attention instantly shifted, making the loud breaking glass the new Focus.


Factors Determining Attention

Paying attention is in general a function of two distinct categories of factors: factors external to the perceiver and factors internal to the perceiver.

A. External Factors (Characteristics of objects/stimuli in the environment):
1. Size and Intensity: Bigger, louder, and brighter stimuli are far more likely to capture your attention than smaller, quieter, and dimmer objects. (e.g., Highway billboards written in gigantic block letters, or a person wearing neon-bright clothing).
2. Repetition: Humans are naturally conditioned to attend to stimuli that repeatedly occur. A misspelled word on a slide is noticed much more quickly if it appears multiple times. Slogans and commercials are repeated continuously to audiences because repetition is inherently attention-getting.
3. Novelty (or newness): Novel, unusual, or unexpected objects create a sharp visual/auditory contrast with the familiar environment. (e.g., Why a foreign guest in a classroom gets immediate special attention, or why unexpected events stand out).
4. Movement: Moving objects tend to capture human attention much faster than static, non-moving objects. Your eyes involuntarily track movement because moving objects were evolutionarily perceived as potential hazards, threats, or prey.

B. Internal Factors (Psychological and physiological states of the observer):
1. Set or Expectancy: A state of mental readiness where an individual is "primed" to detect specific sensory inputs. This varies drastically from person to person based on their current psychological context.
   • Module Example: A father expecting an urgent phone call late at night will instantly awaken to the faint ring of the telephone. His wife, however, may sleep through the phone call but immediately awaken to the faint sound of their baby crying.
2. Motives or Needs: Biological and psychological drive states dictate perceptual selection. People who are extremely hungry, thirsty, or tired will selectively pay attention to environmental cues that offer satisfaction for those pressing internal needs.

👉 ትኩረታችንን የሚወስኑ ነገሮች:
• External (ውጫዊ ምክንያቶች): ከእኛ አእምሮ ውጪ ባሉ ነገሮች ባህሪ የሚወሰኑ ናቸው። ትላልቅና ደማቅ ነገሮች (Size & Intensity)፣ ደጋግመው የሚከሰቱ ድምፆች/ማስታወቂያዎች (Repetition)፣ አዲስና እንግዳ የሆኑ ነገሮች (Novelty)፣ እና የሚንቀሳቀሱ ነገሮች (Movement) ቶሎ ትኩረታችንን ይስባሉ።
• Internal (ውስጣዊ ምክንያቶች): ከራሳችን የስነ-ልቦና እና የአካል ሁኔታ ጋር ይያያዛሉ። Set/Expectancy (የመጠበቅ ስሜት/ዝግጁነት) ካለን ያንን ነገር ቶሎ እንሰማለን (ለምሳሌ፡ የፈተና ውጤት እየጠበቀ ያለ ተማሪ የስልክ መልእክት ድምፅ ቶሎ ይሰማል)። Motives/Needs (የፍላጎት/የረሃብ ሁኔታ) ካሉንም እንደዚሁ፤ በጣም የራበው ተማሪ ቪዥዋል ትኩረቱ ሙሉ በሙሉ ምግብ ቤቶችና የዳቦ ማስታወቂያዎች ላይ ያተኩራል።

😂 የሳይኮሎጂ ቀልድ ለፈገግታ:
አንድ በረሀብ የተቆላ የዩኒቨርሲቲ ተማሪ (Motives/Needs) እና አንድ የልብስ ሱቅ መክፈት የሚያልም ተማሪ (Set/Expectancy) አብረው ከተማ እየዞሩ ነው። በድንገት አንዱ "ዋው! ያንን አየኸው?" ይላል። የልብስ አፍቃሪው "አዎ፣ ያቺ ልጅ የለበሰችው ጃኬት ከለር (External-Intensity) አያምርም!" ሲል... የራበው ተማሪ ግን "ምን ጃኬት? እኔ ያየሁት እኮ ከኋላዋ ያለው የካፌ 'ስጋ ጥብስ አለ' የሚለውን ትልቅ ፅሁፍ (External-Size) ነው!" አለው ይባላል። 😂 (ሁለቱም የራሳቸውን Internal Factor መርጠው ነው Perceive ያደረጉት!)


2.3.2. Form Perception

Visual sensations provide raw, unstructured physical data. Form perception is the cognitive process by which these sensory inputs are organized into meaningful patterns, shapes, structured forms, and identifiable objects. To perceive any form, your visual system must first separate a figure (an object) from its ground (its background surroundings).

1. Figure-Ground Perception
It is the fundamental perceptual organization of visual fields into objects (figures) that stand out prominently against their surroundings (ground).
• Printed words (figure) standing out against a white book page (ground).
• A framed painting (figure) hanging on a solid concrete wall (ground).
• A soloist's singing voice (figure) standing out from the background instrumental chords (ground).
Note: Form perception is an active mental construction. Under specific conditions, a shift can occur where the figure becomes the ground and the ground becomes the figure.

2. Contours in Form Perception
We separate individual forms from their background primarily because our eyes perceive contours. Contours are created whenever there is a marked, abrupt difference in brightness, contrast, or color between an object and its immediate background.
• If you look at a sheet of paper that varies continuously and smoothly in light intensity without sharp edges, you perceive no distinct contour.
• If the change in light intensity or color is sharp and abrupt, your brain instantly perceives a boundary edge (contour).
• Camouflage: Occurs when physical contours are intentionally disrupted or masked visually. Because the marked contrast between the object and background is erased, the object becomes nearly impossible to distinguish from its environment.

👉 Form Perception - ቅርፅን መለየት:
አይናችን የሚያያቸውን ጥሬ ምስሎች አደራጅተን የምንረዳበት መንገድ ነው። ለዚህ ደግሞ ዋናው መነሻ Figure (ዋናው ምስል) እና Ground (ጀርባው/Background) መለየት ነው። ግድግዳ (Ground) ላይ የተሰቀለ ፎቶ (Figure)፣ ወይም ወረቀት (Ground) ላይ ያለ ፅሁፍ (Figure) ግልጽ ምሳሌዎች ናቸው።
• Contours (ድንበሮች/ወሰኖች): አንድን ምስል ከጀርባው ለይተን እንድናውቅ የሚረዳን የከለር ወይም የብርሃን ከፍተኛ መለዋወጥ (Marked difference) ነው። ድንበሩ ከተሸፈነ ወይም ከጀርባው ጋር ተመሳሳይ ከሆነ ምስሉ ከጀርባው ጋር ይቀላቀላል፤ ይሄ Camouflage (ካሜፍላጅ) ይባላል (ለምሳሌ ወታደሮች ጫካ ውስጥ አረንጓዴ ልብስ ሲለብሱ ድንበራቸው/Contours ስለሚሸፈን ከጀርባው ጋር ተዋህደው አይታዩም)።

💡 Exam Hint: ፈተና ላይ "A chameleon changes its skin color to blend with tree leaves" ብሎ ከጠየቃችሁ፣ መልሱ disrupting contours (camouflage) በማድረግ Figure እና Ground እንዳይለያዩ ለማድረግ ነው።


Organization in Form Perception (Gestalt Principles)

When multiple sensory elements are present together in our visual field, we rarely perceive them as separate, disconnected fragments. Instead, our minds automatically group them into organized patterns. The famous Gestalt psychologists thoroughly investigated this phenomenon and established the foundational axiom: "The whole is more than the sum of its parts." This means that the total perceived form possesses unique properties that do not exist in the individual parts alone.

Laws of Perceptual Organization:

1. Proximity (Nearness): Sensory elements that are physically positioned close to one another in space or time are naturally perceived as belonging together as a single unified group.

Visual Aid 2: Law of Proximity

 o  o  o  o        o o   o o
 o  o  o  o        o o   o o
[12 dots]        [2 Columns]


2. Similarity: Items that share similar visual characteristics (such as shape, color, or size) are automatically grouped together in perception.

Visual Aid 3: Law of Similarity
 X  O  X  O
 X  O  X  O
 X  O  X  O
[Perceived as vertical columns of Xs and Os]


3. Good Figure (Symmetry): The psychological tendency to organize visual elements into simple, elegant, balanced, and symmetrical structures. (Note: The law of good figure often dominates over the law of similarity when both compete in a visual field).

4. Continuation: The perceptual tendency to see a line, curve, or motion that starts in a particular direction as continuing smoothly along its established path, rather than breaking abruptly into sharp angles.

5. Closure: The perceptual process that organizes incomplete sensory data by filling in missing gaps in stimulation to construct a complete, whole, and meaningful object.

👉 የGestalt የማደራጀት ህጎች :
Gestalt ሳይኮሎጂስቶች "አንድ ሙሉ ነገር ከክፍፎቹ ድምር ይበልጣል (The whole is more than the sum of its parts)" የሚል ጽንሰ-ሐሳብ አላቸው። አእምሯችን ምስሎችን ሲያይ የተበታተኑ ነጥቦችን ሳይሆን አደራጅቶ ትርጉም ያለው ቅርፅ (Pattern) ያወጣላቸዋል። ህጎቹም፦
1. Proximity (መቀራረብ): በቦታ ወይም በጊዜ ተቀራርበው ያሉ ነገሮችን እንደ አንድ ግሩፕ አድርገን እንረዳለን።
2. Similarity (መመሳሰል): ተመሳሳይ ከለር፣ መጠን ወይም ቅርፅ ያላቸውን ነገሮች አጣጥመን በአንድ ላይ እናያቸዋለን።
3. Good Figure (ሚዛናዊነት/Symmetry): ነገሮችን የተስተካከለ እና ሚዛናዊ (Balanced) በሆነ ቀለል ባለ መንገድ አደራጅቶ የማየት ዝንባሌ ነው።
4. Continuation (ቀጣይነት): አንድ መስመር የጀመረበትን ለስላሳ የትራፊክ መስመር (Smooth curve) ሳያቋርጥ እንደቀጠለ አድርገን መረዳት።
5. Closure (ክፍተትን መሙላት): የተቋረጡ መስመሮችን ወይም ጎደሎ ምስሎችን አእምሯችን ክፍተቱን (Gaps) በምናቡ ሞልቶ ሙሉ ምስል አድርጎ ይረዳዋል።

🤔 Case Question 2:
A teacher draws a triangle on the blackboard using dashed dotted lines with noticeable gaps between the dashes. When she asks the students what shape it is, they all immediately answer "A triangle!" rather than "A series of disconnected dots."
Question: Which Gestalt law of perceptual organization explains the students' response?

Answer: The Law of Closure. The students' visual perception automatically filled in the physical gaps between the dots to form a complete geometric triangle.
